He played [[college basketball]] for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] and [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], with whom in his senior season he led the [[Southeastern Conference]] with a 90.8% [[free throw percentage]]. ==Early life and high school== Hannahs was born and raised in [[Little Rock, Arkansas]] and attended high school at [[Pulaski Academy]]. He was a three-time All-District selection, and was named first team [[Arkansas Activities Association#4A|4A]] All-State in his junior and senior seasons with the Bruins.{{cite web|first=Tye|last=Richardson|title=Dusty Hannahs Comes Back Home|url=http://www.uatrav.com/sports/article_5284fcd6-5e34-11e4-a1e6-001a4bcf6878.html|work=[[The Arkansas Traveler (newspaper)|The Arkansas Traveler]]|date=October 28, 2014|access-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330224934/http://www.uatrav.com/sports/article_5284fcd6-5e34-11e4-a1e6-001a4bcf6878.html|archive-date=March 30, 2019|url-status=live}} He committed to [[Texas Tech University]] after his junior season after averaging 26.2 points per game and shooting 51 percent from three.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kosmider|title=Local basketball standout Schneider signs with Lady Raiders|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/article/20111109/SPORTS/311099752|website=LubbockOnline.com|publisher=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=November 9, 2011|access-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330224933/https://www.lubbockonline.com/article/20111109/SPORTS/311099752|archive-date=March 30, 2019|url-status=live}} In his senior season, Hannahs averaged 20 points per game, and led PA to the 4A state championship game and scored 43 points in a loss to [[Clarksville High School (Arkansas)|Clarksville High School]]. ==College career== ===Texas Tech=== Hannahs began his collegiate career at [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]]. He averaged 6.9 points as a freshman and 7.7 points per game as a sophomore, while appearing mostly as a three-point specialist and [[sixth man]] off the bench.{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Hope|title=Arkansas' most interesting players|url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2017/03/13/arkansas-most-interesting-players-watch/99127100/|work=[[The Anderson Independent-Mail]]|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330221606/https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2017/03/13/arkansas-most-interesting-players-watch/99127100/|archive-date=March 30, 2019|url-status=live}} He set the Texas Tech season record for [[free throw percentage]] with 92.3 in his sophomore season. Following the end of the season, Hannahs announced that he would be transferring to the [[University of Arkansas]].{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Magelssen|title=Former Texas Tech guard Dusty Hannahs announces he will transfer to Arkansas|url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/texastechredraiders/2014/04/10/former-texas-tech-guard-dusty-hannahs-announces-he-will-transfer-to-arkansas|website=SportsDay.DallasNews.com|publisher=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=April 10, 2014|access-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330221608/https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/texastechredraiders/2014/04/10/former-texas-tech-guard-dusty-hannahs-announces-he-will-transfer-to-arkansas|archive-date=March 30, 2019|url-status=live}} ===Arkansas=== Hannahs played for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] for the final two seasons of his eligibility after sitting out one year due to [[NCAA]] transfer rules. In his first season with the team, Hannahs led the Razorbacks with 16.5 points per game (8th in the SEC), had a .458 field goal percentage (8th), and led the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) with 81 three pointers made, and .870 free throw percentage, and a .433 three-point percentage.{{cite web|title=Dusty Hannahs College Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dusty-hannahs-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=December 20, 2024}} He was named to the [[Jerry West Award]] watchlist going into his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] senior season.{{cite web|first=Less|last=Moore|title=Hannahs on Prestigious Watch List|url=https://www.fox16.com/sports/local-sports/hannahs-on-prestigious-watch-list/596726930|website=FOX16.com|publisher=[[KLRT-TV]]|date=October 18, 2016|access-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330223107/https://www.fox16.com/sports/local-sports/hannahs-on-prestigious-watch-list/596726930|archive-date=March 30, 2019|url-status=live}} Hannahs again led Arkansas in scoring in his final season with 14.4 points per game and led the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) with a 90.8% [[free throw percentage]] (10th-best in the nation) and was named second team All-SEC by ''[[NBC Sports|NBCSports.com]]''.{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Muck|title=Former Pulaski Academy, UA standout Dusty Hannahs still after pro dream|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2019/feb/12/hannahs-still-after-pro-dream-20190212/|website=ArkansasOnline.com|publisher=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=February 12, 2019|url-status=live}} He scored 1,047 points for the Razorbacks, becoming the fifth Arkansas player to score 1,000 points in two seasons, and finished ninth in school history with 155 three pointers ==Professional career== ===Memphis Hustle / Grizzlies (2017–2020)=== Hannahs originally committed to play overseas for [[AZS Koszalin]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]], but ultimately opted to sign with the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]] on October 6, 2017.{{cite web|first=Otis|last=Kirk|title=Former Razorback lands in NBA's G League with Memphis|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/article/former-arkansas-razorback-dusty-hannahs-lands-in-nbas-g-league-with-memphis-hustle-108498779/|website=247Sports.com|date=October 6, 9, 2023|url-status=live}} In his first professional season, Hannahs appeared mostly as the Hustle's sixth man and averaged 9.2 points per game while shooting 44.1 percent on three point shots and 90.5 percent from the free throw line. Hannahs returned to the Hustle for a second season and was the only player on from the previous year's team on the roster.{{cite web|first=Bob|last=Bakken|title=Hustle training camp
